claims.text: CoCrNiV is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Fine-grained Co33Cr24Ni33V10 can retain a single-phase FCC structure after rolling, heat treatment, and tensile deformation.
A fully recrystallized fine-grained CoCrNiV alloy can have a mean grain size near 0.95 micrometers.
The fine-grained FCC CoCrNiV baseline has a yield strength of approximately 1060 MPa.
The fine-grained FCC CoCrNiV baseline has approximately 24% uniform elongation.
The baseline CoCrNiV alloy deforms primarily through dislocation slip and stacking faults without twinning or phase transformation.
Interstitial oxygen occupies or migrates between interstitial lattice sites in NiCoCr.
Interstitial oxygen doping raises the stacking-fault energy of CoCrNiV.
The oxygen-induced increase in stacking-fault energy is modest at the proposed low doping level.
Increasing stacking-fault energy through oxygen doping suppresses deformation twinning and promotes dislocation glide.
A deformation mode dominated by uniform dislocation glide improves ductility and uniform deformability.
Low-level oxygen doping will significantly increase uniform elongation and improve strain hardening relative to untreated CoCrNiV.
Low-level oxygen doping will preserve the yield strength of CoCrNiV.
Low-level oxygen doping will preserve impact-induced energy release.
Low-level oxygen doping will preserve impact energy absorption.
The proposed oxygen-doping effect will hold under room-temperature quasi-static tensile and impact loading.
Higher oxygen concentrations may cause unwanted phase transformations or degraded mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The central claim concerns preserving impact-induced energy release, but the predicted outcome and experiment measure impact energy absorption. Energy release and absorbed impact energy are distinct quantities, so the proposed experiment does not directly test the stated energetic-performance claim.
